studies.Population: Japan Public Health Center-based Prospective Study participants who reported no history of cancer
studies.Ethnicity Basis: NA: no field-specific ethnicity evidence was available
studies.Reference: Sugary drink consumption and risk of kidney and bladder cancer in Japanese adults.
studies.Authors: Leung CY, Abe SK, Sawada N, Ishihara J, Takachi R, Yamaji T, Iwasaki M, Hashizume M, Inoue M, Tsugane S
studies.Timing: Exposure assessed at baseline (1995-1999); follow-up to December 31, 2013, excluding cases in first three years
studies.comparison_type: per 100 ml/day increase in sugary drink consumption
studies.exposure_measurement_supporting_text: Sugary drink consumption was assessed using a validated food frequency questionnaire

sample_size.excerpt: We examined the association of sugary drinks with risk of kidney and bladder cancer in 73,024 participants from the Japan Public Health Center-based Prospective Study who reported no history of cancer.

cases.excerpt: During 1,069,815 person years of follow-up, 169 kidney cancer and 297 bladder cancer cases were documented.

effect_size.excerpt: However, sugary drink consumption was positively associated with the risk of kidney cancer (HR for 100 ml/day increase in consumption was 1.11 [95% CI 1.01-1.22]) and bladder cancer (HR for 100 ml/d increase in consumption was 1.11 [95% CI 1.01-1.22]) among women after exclusion of cases diagnosed in the first three years of follow-up.

confidence_interval.excerpt: However, sugary drink consumption was positively associated with the risk of kidney cancer (HR for 100 ml/day increase in consumption was 1.11 [95% CI 1.01-1.22]) and bladder cancer (HR for 100 ml/d increase in consumption was 1.11 [95% CI 1.01-1.22]) among women after exclusion of cases diagnosed in the first three years of follow-up.

comparison.excerpt: HR for 100 ml/d increase in consumption

timing.excerpt: Sugary drink consumption was assessed using a validated food frequency questionnaire at study baseline (1995-1999). Individuals were followed to December 31, 2013.

continent.excerpt: Japan Public Health Center-based Prospective Study
